items.stem: Why can an AI risk assessment be inadequate without a separate impact assessment for a public-sector decision tool?

options.text: Risk assessment often centres on the organisation's risk, while impact assessment centres on harms to affected people and groups
options.rationale: Correct: impact assessment foregrounds effects on individuals and society.

options.text: They are identical, so one is redundant
options.rationale: They have different focuses and are not interchangeable.

options.text: Impact assessments are only for cybersecurity
options.rationale: Impact assessment covers harms broadly, not only security.

options.text: Risk assessment is only for hardware
options.rationale: Risk assessment applies to AI systems generally.

items.explanation: Correct: impact assessment foregrounds effects on individuals and society.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO inputs most improve the quality of an AI harm identification? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Input from people representative of the affected groups
options.rationale: Correct: affected-group perspectives surface harms designers miss.

options.text: A structured taxonomy of known AI harms to prompt the team
options.rationale: Correct: a taxonomy helps surface categories that would be overlooked.
A single-perspective team misses many harms.
Self-reported confidence does not identify harms.

items.explanation: Correct: affected-group perspectives surface harms designers miss.

items.stem: Two risks both score 'high'. What is the best way to prioritise between them?

options.text: Examine severity, reversibility and who is affected, and record the rationale
options.rationale: Correct: structured tie-breaking on severity and affected parties is defensible.

options.text: Pick whichever is cheaper to fix
options.rationale: Cost alone is not a defensible harm priority.

options.text: Address neither until a metric separates them
options.rationale: Judgement with documented rationale is expected.
The colour is the output, not a tie-breaker.

items.explanation: Correct: structured tie-breaking on severity and affected parties is defensible.
